A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MERIT dataset and CORAL framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V2 reports original retrieval experiments, CORAL ablations, out-of-distribution evaluations and a human preference study, including Tables 2–3 and 7–12.

after.justification: V3 retains the original retrieval experiments, ablations, out-of-distribution results and human preference study in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 retains CORAL’s contrastive learning, masked visual and language reconstruction, and query/target EOS-based reconstruction. The dataset-construction procedures in Appendix A are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five-language MERIT coverage, eight auxiliary retrieval tasks, FashionIQ/CIRR visual-necessity evaluations and language, attribute and product-class OOD scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same zero-shot and embedding models in Table 2, retrieval baselines in Table 10, and human-preference and condition-count comparators in Tables 11–12.

E3.justification: The 310,000/10,000 training/test split, recall and MRR metrics, model configurations, single-epoch training, OOD exclusions and human-study design remain unchanged in Sections 3 and E.1–E.7.

E4.justification: Both retain the reconstruction, input-type and LoRA ablations; visual-necessity and OOD tests; dataset analyses and examples; error cases; and condition-count analysis. Their relocation adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Point estimates and human-study average selection rates use the same reporting practices. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains CORAL’s 69.68 R@1 and 78.33 MRR, and Table 11 retains its 58.9% Choice@3 selection rate.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–5 retain the same content. Differences are typographical; no assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset contribution, diagnosis of neglected conditional information and CORAL contribution. The 45.9% improvement claim and validation across eight retrieval tasks are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning visual necessity, sequential-image processing and attribute errors remain unchanged. Appendix F retains the qualifications about category imbalance, cultural and attribute biases, and image–text inconsistencies.

D1.justification: V3 adds explicit GitHub repository and Hugging Face dataset links on the first page; v2 supplies only the project-page link. This expands access information without establishing newly available resources. Appendix implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 109 works and retain their research-positioning arguments. Reference reordering, citation renumbering and bibliographic formatting changes do not alter the cited research.

P1.justification: Limited wording and CORAL styling edits accompany a new Appendix heading and movement of References from before the appendices to the end. The substantive narrative and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V3 introduces a shaded title/abstract/link panel and new icons, changes typography and caption styling throughout, and extensively resizes and relocates figures and tables. Appendix examples are redistributed across pages, while the scientific graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 replaces v2’s split abstract with a complete first-page abstract and adds direct repository and dataset links. These changes modestly improve readability and access guidance. The extensive visual redesign preserves the method, experimental evidence and stated limitations, so the overall gain is limited.
